audit.whatIsWrong: Five rows disagreed across layers. Full-layer phases[].side read Orianna/Orianna/Orianna/Skill/Skill/Skill/Ryze while content win[] read Orianna/Skill/Skill/Orianna/Orianna/Skill/Orianna - most seriously the 2+ items row, where the full layer handed the late game to Ryze and the content layer handed it to Orianna.
audit.why: The content layer matches the packet levelChart. Levels 2-3 are a real fight because Spell Flux is on 3.5s and turns Rune Prison into a root; levels 4-6 are Orianna's once you can stay clean of the orb and Shockwave punishes any step-up on the 11s W downtime; two-plus items are Orianna's because Ryze's chain is single-target against a five-man Shockwave and a shielded line.
audit.corrected: Full layer moved onto the content values with ratings 7/5/5/6/6/6/7 on the moved rows, whys rewritten in the same proposal.

audit.why: The spike map is sound: Ryze's real lane spike is first item plus rune stacks, not level 6 - Realm Warp (180/160/140, 3000 range) creates a portal for allies and is a rotation tool, so it does not spike the lane at all. Orianna's level 6 and two-item teamfight spikes are correctly placed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction in this matchup was stated nowhere: Rune Prison only ROOTS if the target already has Spell Flux on them - otherwise it is a slow. The page called the ability "Rune Prison (Root)" throughout as if the root were unconditional. breakdown.cooldowns also held no digit.
audit.why: Riot's W text: he traps a target in a cage of runes, damaging and slowing them; if the target has Flux on it, they are instead rooted. Spell Flux is 3.5s at rank 1 and 615 range, so the whole lane is about whether the orb is on you when the cage lands. Overload is 1000 range on a 5s cooldown that his other casts reset.
audit.corrected: tldr, winCon, enemyWin, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d and the moved whys now state the Flux-then-root condition and carry 11s, 3.5s, 5s, 615 and 1000.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three content fields called Overload short-ranged: whys[0] "short-cast Overload", spikes[0].text "short-range Overload", and early "Ryze's short Overload". The advice built on that told you to out-range him.
audit.why: Overload is 1000 range. Orianna's Command: Attack is 815. Ryze out-ranges Orianna on that ability, so "you out-range him" is backwards. The genuine edge is that Overload damages only the first enemy struck, so the minion wave eats it, while Orianna's ball travels through and lands where she puts it.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten around the first-target-only behaviour rather than a range advantage that does not exist.

notes: Two substantive factual corrections here. First, the page labelled the ability "Rune Prison (Root)" everywhere as though the root were unconditional; Riot's text says it slows, and only roots if the target already has Spell Flux. That conditional is the whole matchup and it was absent. The focus.text field still reads "Ryze Rune Prison (Root)" and the loading line repeats it - I did not edit those because the (Effect) naming convention is documented as correct and I could not tell whether the applier treats focus.text as an enum; it should probably become "Ryze Spell Flux" since that is the ability you actually dodge. See questionsForUser. Second, three content fields called Overload short-ranged and told the reader to out-range it: Overload is 1000 and Command: Attack is 815, so that was backwards; rewritten around Overload hitting only the first enemy struck. Cross-layer chart disagreement fixed on rows 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6; win[N] already holds the correct value on disk so no paired edits are proposed.
